name: Name-That-Hash - Modern Hash Type Identifier
description: Name-That-Hash identifies hash types and provides the corresponding hashcat mode and John format. More accurate and actively maintained than hashid. Supports all common hash types including NTLM, Kerberoast, AS-REP, bcrypt, and application-specific hashes. Essential before cracking unknown hashes.
notes:
=== INSTALL ===
  pip install name-that-hash
  # Or: pip3 install name-that-hash

=== IDENTIFY SINGLE HASH ===
  nth -t "5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
  # Output: MD5 (hashcat: 0, john: raw-md5)

  nth -t "$krb5tgs$23$*user$domain$..."
  # Output: Kerberos 5 TGS-REP (hashcat: 13100)

  nth -t "aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:31d6cfe0d16ae931b73c59d7e0c089c0"
  # Output: NTLM (hashcat: 1000)

=== IDENTIFY FROM FILE ===
  nth -f hashes.txt
  # Identifies each hash in the file

=== COMMON HASH TYPES ===
  MD5:         32 hex chars          hashcat -m 0
  SHA1:        40 hex chars          hashcat -m 100
  SHA256:      64 hex chars          hashcat -m 1400
  NTLM:        32 hex chars          hashcat -m 1000
  NTLMv2:      includes ::           hashcat -m 5600
  Kerberoast:  $krb5tgs$23$          hashcat -m 13100
  AS-REP:      $krb5asrep$23$        hashcat -m 18200
  bcrypt:      $2a$ or $2b$          hashcat -m 3200
  DCC2:        $DCC2$                hashcat -m 2100
  NetNTLMv1:   includes :::          hashcat -m 5500

=== VS hashid ===
  nth: More accurate, shows hashcat mode AND john format
  hashid: Older, sometimes misidentifies, no hashcat modes

recommended.note: hashid is the older alternative; nth is more accurate.
After identifying the hash type, crack with hashcat.

defense.why_it_works: Hash identification is a passive, offline operation. It analyzes the format and structure of hash strings to determine the algorithm used.
defense.prerequisites: Hash string to identify; name-that-hash installed.
defense.impact: Identifies hash algorithms enabling targeted cracking attacks.
defense.artifacts: name-that-hash in process list on attacker machine only.
defense.prevention: Use strong hashing algorithms (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2); salt all hashes; enforce strong passwords.
